criteria.evidence: The test approved_rejected_and_within_limit_proposals_leave_nothing_waiting passed. It builds a Snapshot with two decided ids (approved and rejected) and one steward proposal at DefaultsConventions with the steward's limit at DefaultsConventions. It asserts 'Nothing waiting for you' is present, '' is absent. The decided proposals are marked through the `decided` set, not through WorkDecision values; that is acceptable at the Snapshot level. findings.summary: The root cause of approved and rejected proposals showing on the published page is neither found, fixed nor named; for decided proposals the change only moves an existing filter.
findings.evidence: In the old code, read_snapshot already ran `proposals.retain(|p| !decided.contains(&p.item.id));` (the line removed in the diff), and the old test the_page_links_every_record_to_github_at_the_tip_and_lists_only_open_proposals already checked it. Moving the check into render() changes nothing for decided proposals. So whatever made qyd9 (approved) and jtd2 (rejected) show on 3 Nov is untouched. Reading the code suggests a stale page: crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs approve_work/reject_work commit the decision to the records branch at once, but .github/workflows/pages.yml rebuilds decisions.html only on `push: branches: [main]`. The other possibility is that the decision records are missing from the branch. Neither can be checked in this snapshot, which has no records/. The workflow is out of scope, so the root-cause rule required naming the cause and proposing a fix. The CHANGELOG line names no cause, while nearby entries ('Root cause: ...') do. The reading's assumptions also asked the producer for this.

findings.summary: The within-limit check copies in_limit() from athena-core instead of sharing one definition.
findings.evidence: `role_limit(..).is_some_and(|limit| may_change(limit, rung))` is the same as athena_core::work_decisions::in_limit and split_open. xtask depends only on athena-data, athena-git and athena-context, so the copy is understandable, but the two rules can drift apart. Moving the predicate into athena-data would let both use it.

findings.summary: The records-branch test would also pass on the old code, so it shows no fix for decided proposals.
findings.evidence: The proposals in this test are above the scribe's Implementation limit, and the old read_snapshot already dropped decided ones. The test satisfies criterion 3 but does not catch the problem the user reported.

summary: The change hides proposals the steward could approve itself, uses the one-line "Nothing waiting for you" empty state, and adds the three requested tests. `cargo test -p xtask decisions` passed all 13 tests here, and Athena's CI records show fmt, clippy and tests passing. All seven criteria are met. It still fails, on the root-cause rule. Most of what the user reported was that approved and rejected proposals stayed on the published page, and the change does not alter that. The old code already dropped any proposal named by an approve or reject record; the change only moves that same check into render(). So whatever made 20261016-055247-qyd9 and 20261017-204324-jtd2 show on 3 Nov is neither found nor named. Reading the code points to a stale page: approve-work and reject-work write to the records branch at once, but pages.yml rebuilds decisions.html only on a push to main. Missing decision records are the other possibility; neither can be checked here because records/ is not in this snapshot. Only the within-limit proposal (20261018-000648-ne91) is actually fixed.
